analysis.title: GS DeGrasse - Desk Bank/Fins EPS Preview 7 Oct 2026
key_insights: Financials EPS season starts Tuesday with JPM, C and WFC reporting in the morning. The desk's focus list: capital markets trading normalization after a strong 2Q26, NII, deposit costs, loan growth, expenses, capital, credit, consumer, and agentic AI.
Capital markets question: how much trading normalizes after a strong 2Q26, and whether 3Q26 investment banking was an air pocket or the start of a longer slowdown.

NII outlooks are being reset for a sharp rise in rates and a more hawkish forward curve. Strong asset growth and fixed-rate asset repricing are weighed against rising deposit costs. A deposit beta lag could help 4Q26 net interest margins.
Capital: less excess capital, strong loan growth and higher rates hitting AOCI raise the chance of more buyback pauses at regional banks (similar to USB) or a slower pace at the money-center banks.
Credit is benign going into the prints, which supports potential reserve releases. The desk is watching whether the rate move creates early stress, with focus on multifamily CRE.
Consumer: the desk asks how higher oil prices and rates have weighed on consumer health and spending.

Agentic AI is a debate across banks, retail brokers and wealth, personal insurance and payments. The desk asks whether it will be addressed on earnings calls and what it means for deposits, funding costs, profitability and customer growth.
Large bank sentiment is mixed. The sector has often been a source of funds for money leaving Financials or rotating to nonbanks.

Regional banks: positioning is down from early summer highs, but hedge funds have been buying since the mid-quarter conferences on a view of near-term upside to 4Q numbers. The desk calls the buying somewhat tactical, with 2027 still debated.
Consumer finance is notably negative among both hedge funds and long-only investors. The stated reason is that the cycle is not early and oil poses a tail risk, which keeps multiples contained.
Payments sentiment is warm. The group is increasingly viewed as insulated from agentic AI or a winner, and spend trends improved into the end of 3Q.

Boutique investment banks are among the lowest-sentiment groups with specialists. Near-term numbers are falling on the 3Q activity air pocket, and there are fears boutiques have limited levers on compensation and non-compensation costs to support margins.

Life insurance has seen an uptick in long-only interest on higher rates, a positive equity market and a desire for single-digit P/E stocks without a perceived AI link. Commercial carriers and reinsurers and personal insurance remain negative from specialists on pricing.

Hedge fund exposure to US Financials has rebounded from the start of last EPS season and enters the quarter around 3-year averages. The US bank long/short ratio fell sharply across large caps and regionals, the insurance ratio rose quarter over quarter, and the consumer finance ratio is near 2-year lows.

Financials come into earnings after sharply underperforming the S&P 500. September was rough: Financials closed lower on 16 of 21 sessions, tied for the worst month since November 1999. The 4th quarter has historically been favorable seasonally.

Earnings reaction history: JPM had the best reaction in the large cap bank group in 2 of the last 16 quarters. MS has traded higher in 9 of its last 10 prints. WFC has traded lower on 9 of the last 13. BLK has rallied after 7 of its last 8 prints, averaging +4.3% in those 7.

earnings_insights: Bank earnings season begins Tuesday (JPM, C, WFC before the open). This is a preview of focus questions, with no reported or estimated EPS figures.
BAC: whether NII upside updated for the rate curve can flow into operating leverage, and trading outlook relative to peers.
WFC: near-term NIM and deposit costs, and where FY26 NII settles versus the $50bn target.
JPM: how to think about 2027 operating leverage, and whether the call clarifies both NII and expenses or only one.
C: how front-loaded 2H26 investments affect 2027 expenses, efficiency and returns.

KEY: whether a 3.25% NIM is still achievable. HBAN: whether near-term estimates are derisked after the guidance reset at the September industry conference. ALLY: NIM path given the hawkish curve shift, and credit trajectory into 2027.

SCHW: higher-rate tailwinds to NII versus potential changes in balance sheet and cash. AMG: whether tax-aware growth is slowing given recent headlines. AMP: margin and growth profile given press reports of potential retention packages.

HIG: potential for additional reserve action in General Liability and Commercial Auto, and the disability loss ratio. WTW: whether strong R&B organic growth continues after 2Q and whether margin can deliver the expected 100bps average annual gain.
TOST: whether 2027 numbers are derisked, weighing ARPU upside against competition concerns. V and MA: confidence in 2027 growth and the valuation spread between the two.

Post-earnings price reaction history: WFC traded lower on 9 of the last 13 prints, but averaged +5.5% on the 4 it traded higher. USB traded lower after 9 of its last 12. PNC moved less than +/-1% on 4 of its last 8. COF has traded lower 3 straight quarters after 13 straight positive reactions. AXP traded lower in 12 of its last 16, but its 4 up prints were the largest moves, averaging +7.85%.
crypto_views: Crypto trading: the desk asks whether activity is inflecting or the recent pickup is a flash in the pan.
Market structure: the desk asks how companies view tokenization (institutional adoption) and new products such as event contracts and perpetual futures.
risk_factors: Rates: a sharp rise and a more hawkish forward curve could pressure capital markets, sponsor activity, CRE transactions and debt issuance, and raise deposit costs.
Credit: early stress from higher rates, especially in multifamily CRE.
Consumer: higher oil prices and rates weighing on consumer health.
Capital: higher rates hitting AOCI, less excess capital and more buyback pauses.
Capital markets: a prolonged slowdown after the 3Q26 air pocket in activity.
Personal insurance: possibly high 3Q storm losses and pricing pressure.
Agentic AI: the competitive and margin implications for banks, brokers, insurers and customer acquisition.
vol_and_positioning: Hedge fund exposure to US Financials rebounded from the start of last EPS season and is around 3-year averages.
The US bank long/short ratio fell sharply across large cap and regional banks, with some rotation into regionals ahead of earnings.
The US insurance long/short ratio rose quarter over quarter, and the US consumer finance long/short ratio is near 2-year lows.

Desk scorecard context: BAC sentiment changed significantly at the mid-quarter conference. PGR is viewed very differently on agentic AI. SCHW is a battleground with vocal bulls and bears. TRV is debated, with long-onlys leaning bullish and hedge funds leaning bearish.

Alternative asset manager positioning swings sharply with rates. Traditional asset managers are favored by hedge funds with little long-only sponsorship, and systematic over active is a popular trade.
